turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll type END MEETING on its own line, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have a client call at 4:40, so we have about twenty minutes. Before we start: who decided to give my son a zero, and did anyone speak to him first?
The checker said 94 percent. That's the end of it.

"The end of it." Okay, I'm writing that down, along with your own procedure 4.3, which says detection software does not by itself establish a concern. So unless you have something I can actually read, I'm going to the principal's office when we're done here.
I don't need more proof than that.

"You don't need more proof." Then you've just told me the zero rests on a machine's guess and nothing else, and the company that sells it says not to do exactly that. Withdraw the zero today, Hale, or I take this upstairs.
The software doesn't lie, unlike some people.
My son does not lie. Are you calling me one too, Hale? Choose your next sentence carefully, because I'm writing down every word.

Then hear what happens next. I walk from this room to the principal's office, and if the zero isn't gone by Friday, I file an appeal with the board under section 42. Owen has a scholarship deadline on December 1, and I won't watch this school do it to a second one of my children.
